issue.title: Prompts that declare input: fail at launch when the body uses agent-run Jinja variables (patch_name, n, wait, agents, ...)

task_type_fields.impact:
Anyone who adds `input:` frontmatter to a prompt, or saves a prompt with inputs, silently
loses every agent-run Jinja variable. The failure only shows at launch, as a
PromptInputError toast, not while editing, and nothing in the docs explains it. The
Jinja-completion epic being planned now has to hide these names in input-declaring
top-level prompts, via an `unavailable` availability state with this reason, so it does
not suggest variables that break the launch. Fixing this bead should drop that
availability rule, which is a single catalog condition in sase-core's jinja catalog. A
fix must keep inputs usable inside `%directives`, which are parsed at launch, while
deferring run-time names to the agent-run render. Candidates are partial rendering
with a preserving Undefined for catalog run-time names, or protecting tags that
reference run-time names.
task_type_fields.repro:
Repro (any sase checkout, no agent needed):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -c "
from sase.agent.prompt_inputs import render_prompt_with_inputs
p='---\ninput:\n  topic: word\n---\nResearch {{ topic }} for {{ patch_name }}\n'
render_prompt_with_inputs(p, {'topic': 'x'})
"
```

Result: `PromptInputError: XPrompt '#prompt-input' template error: 'patch_name' is undefined`.

Root cause: when a top-level prompt declares frontmatter `input:`, the TUI launch path
(`ace/tui/actions/agent_workflow/_launch_prompt_inputs.py`) calls
`render_prompt_with_inputs`. That renders the whole body with StrictUndefined through
`substitute_placeholders` -> `_render_jinja2_template`. The context has only
`get_global_template_vars()` (`root`, plus runtime vars only when bound, and they are not
bound at TUI launch) plus the declared input values. Every agent-run variable is
therefore undefined at that point: `patch_name`, `cl_name`, `workspace_num`, `n`/`N`
(%repeat), `wait`/`wait.chats`/`wait.artifacts`, `wait_chats`, and `agents`. The launch
fails even though the same names render fine in a prompt that declares no inputs,
because that prompt is rendered later inside the agent run with `_build_named_args` in
scope.

issue.creation_reason: Found while designing Jinja variable completion: completion must not suggest names that break launch, and this limitation is undocumented and only surfaces as a launch-time error.
